name: The elders with idols in the temple (Ezekiel 8)
charge: The image of jealousy at the gate; seventy ancients with censers before creeping things and idols portrayed on the wall in the dark, saying, the Lord seeth us not; women weeping for Tammuz; twenty-five men with their backs to the temple worshipping the sun toward the east
summary: Ezekiel was carried in the visions of God to Jerusalem and shown the abominations inside the Lord’s house: an image of jealousy at the gate, seventy elders burning incense before idols painted on the walls of a dark chamber, women at the north gate weeping for Tammuz, and twenty-five men with their backs to the temple bowing to the sun (Ezekiel 8:3-16). The elders said the Lord did not see them; the Lord said these things drove Him from His sanctuary and He would deal in fury and not spare, and the glory departed from the city (Ezekiel 8:12; Ezekiel 8:18; Ezekiel 11:22-23).
offenseFull: In the sixth year, as the elders of Judah sat before Ezekiel in the captivity, the spirit carried him in the visions of God to Jerusalem (Ezekiel 8:1-3). One class says those elders sat before him like they were so righteous; the history teaching notes that the vision shows those not yet taken, for the captivity came in waves. The class on religious syncretism builds up to the chapter through Jeroboam’s calves and Manasseh’s idols in the Lord’s house (2 Kings 21:1-9): we went crazier. At the gate stood the image of jealousy, and the Lord asked whether he saw the great abominations that drove Him far from His own sanctuary (Ezekiel 8:5-6). The Lord is saying, the class says, I cannot be around you all.

Ezekiel dug through the wall and saw every form of creeping thing, abominable beasts and all the idols of the house of Israel painted on the wall round about (Ezekiel 8:7-10). The class sets beside it the images of Cesare Borgia and Guadalupe on the walls today, what we grew up with in the stained glass of the churches

(Deuteronomy 4:16-19). When Judah saw the Chaldeans painted in vermilion she doted on them and sent messengers to them (Ezekiel 23:14-16); the study note says she was drawn in by the flashy art as a harlot is enticed, and the class joins it to the fringes of the law, given so they would not go whoring after their own eyes (Numbers 15:39). Seventy of the elders of Israel stood before those pictures, Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan among them, each with his censer and a thick cloud of incense, saying the Lord did not see them and had forsaken the earth (Ezekiel 8:11-12). The elders were the instructors, one class says, and in the dark they were not even serving God. What do you do in the dark? Your secrets. Men loved darkness rather than light because their deeds were evil (John 3:19); the study note says a man can be comfortable in the darkness he was raised in, and refusing to change is what condemns him.

Then greater abominations: at the north gate women sat weeping for Tammuz (Ezekiel 8:13-14). Israelite women were weeping for Tammuz, the class says. The teachers name Tammuz the son of Nimrod and Semiramis, his mother-wife, the mother and child of the old Babylonian religion carried from Babel into every nation as Isis and Osiris and the Madonna; they call him today baby Jesus, the forever baby, born at the winter solstice, December 25th. Tammuz is what you all celebrate on Christmas, one teacher says. Other classes name his mother Ashtaroth or Astarte; all make him the Babylonian mother-and-child god. In the inner court about twenty-five men stood with their backs to the temple and their faces to the east, worshipping the sun (Ezekiel 8:15-16). Where do you think you get your Sunday service from, one teacher asks: sun worship. They had also filled the land with violence and put the branch to their nose (Ezekiel 8:17), which one class reads as a lit branch that got them high.
judgmentFull: The Lord answered with one sentence: He would deal in fury, His eye would not spare, and though they cried in His ears with a loud voice He would not hear them (Ezekiel 8:18). The men who said the Lord did not see were shown to Him one by one. The eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, the teacher reads (Ecclesiasticus 23:19), and He sets our secret sins in the light of His face (Psalm 90:8). God starts first with the leaders, another class says, and an idol can be anything set before Him, even your children.

The next chapter is the end result of this one, the history teaching says: the mark was set on the foreheads of those who sighed and cried over the abominations, and the slaughter began at the sanctuary, with the elders before the house (Ezekiel 9:1-6). To sigh and cry you must know the law, one class adds (Isaiah 8:16). The glory of the God of Israel went up from the midst of the city and stood on the mountain on the east side, and the spirit carried Ezekiel back to the captives in Chaldea, where he told them everything the Lord had shown him (Ezekiel 11:22-25). The classes bring it home at the season of Tammuz: we were born right here in Babylon the great.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
Do not set up idols in your heart, for it will cause you to stumble into iniquity.
You shall not bring a graven image or other such abomination into your house.
Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
We are not to learn or follow the ways, customs or abominations of the heathen or of any ungodly nation.
You shall not worship the LORD your God in the manner that the heathen nations serve their gods.

text.text: And he put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate that looketh toward the north; where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy.
And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the vision that I saw in the plain.

Then said he unto me, Son of man, lift up thine eyes now the way toward the north. So I lifted up mine eyes the way toward the north, and behold northward at the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry.

He said furthermore unto me, Son of man, seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? but turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations.
And he brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold a hole in the wall.
Then said he unto me, Son of man, dig now in the wall: and when I had digged in the wall, behold a door.
And he said unto me, Go in, and behold the wicked abominations that they do here.
So I went in and saw; and behold every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.

And there stood before them seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel, and in the midst of them stood Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, with every man his censer in his hand; and a thick cloud of incense went up.

Then said he unto me, Son of man, hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.
He said also unto me, Turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations that they do.
Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord’s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.
Then said he unto me, Hast thou seen this, O son of man? turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations than these.

And he brought me into the inner court of the Lord’s house, and, behold, at the door of the temple of the Lord, between the porch and the altar, were about five and twenty men, with their backs toward the temple of the Lord, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east.

Then said he unto me, Son of man, hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.

Then I beheld, and lo a likeness as the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, as the appearance of brightness, as the colour of amber.

Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hephzi–bah.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, after the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord cast out before the children of Israel.

For he built up again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed; and he reared up altars for Baal, and made a grove, as did Ahab king of Israel; and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.
And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord said, In Jerusalem will I put my name.
And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

And he made his son pass through the fire, and observed times, and used enchantments, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards: he wrought much wickedness in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.

And he set a graven image of the grove that he had made in the house, of which the Lord said to David, and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever:

Neither will I make the feet of Israel move any more out of the land which I gave their fathers; only if they will observe to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the law that my servant Moses commanded them.
But they hearkened not: and Manasseh seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel.
